message.content:
Based on my search, here are the key food temperature standards for accepting and handling food safely:

## The Temperature Danger Zone

The most critical concept is the **"temperature danger zone"** — the range where bacteria multiply rapidly:

- **US standards (FDA/USDA)**: 40°F to 140°F (4°C to 60°C)
- **ServSafe**: 41°F to 135°F (5°C to 57°C)
- **Australian standards**: 5°C to 60°C

Food should **NOT** be left in this zone for extended periods. Bacteria can double every 20 minutes in this range.

## Safe Temperatures for Accepting/Holding Food

| Food Type | Safe Temperature |
|-----------|----------------|
| **Cold foods** | 40°F (4°C) or below |
| **Hot foods** | 135°F (57°C) or above |
| **Frozen foods** | 0°F (-18°C) or below |

## Receiving/Accepting Food Deliveries

When accepting food deliveries, you should verify:

- **Cold foods** arrive at **40°F (4°C) or below**
- **Hot foods** arrive at **135°F (57°C) or above** (some standards say 140°F/60°C)
- **Frozen foods** are solid with no signs of thawing

## Safe Cooking/Internal Temperatures

| Food | Minimum Internal Temperature |
|------|------------------------------|
| Poultry, stuffing, dishes with cooked TCS food | 165°F (74°C) |
| Ground meat, injected meats, eggs held for service | 155°F (68°C) |
| Seafood, steaks, chops, roast meats | 145°F (63°C) |
| Vegetables, fruits, grains, legumes | 135°F (57°C) |
| Reheated food | 165°F (74°C) |

## Time Limits in the Danger Zone

- **Cold food** held without refrigeration: maximum **6 hours** (if starting from 40°F and not exceeding 70°F)
- **Hot food** below 135°F: discard after **4 hours**
- **General rule**: Food should not be in the danger zone for more than **2 hours** (or **1 hour** if above 90°F/32°C ambient temperature)

## Key Takeaway

For food acceptance, **reject any delivery** where:
- Cold foods are above 40°F (4°C)
- Hot foods are below 135°F (57°C)
- Frozen foods show signs of thawing or are above 0°F (-18°C)

Sources:
1. https://www.webstaurantstore.com/article/29/following-food-safety-temperatures.html
2. https://thermolog.com.au/australian-food-safety-standards-a-guide-to-temperature-compliance/
3. https://ladle.com/resources/blog/safe-food-temperatures-protect-public-health-and-your-bottom-line/
4. https://www.tempcontrolpack.com/knowledge/temperature-standards-for-coldchain-logistics/
5. https://dutyfront.com/legal-standards-for-food-storage-temperature/
6. https://www.rotomouldedproducts.com/news/what-are-the-key-temperature-requirements-for-safe-food-transportation-according-to-international-st-244097.html
